target.text: How a team does over its next 8 games: the average point margin, adjusted for how strong each opponent was and where the game was played.

factors.label: Elo rating
factors.description: Game-by-game strength rating; wins against good teams by big margins move it most

factors.label: Season record
factors.description: This season's regular-season win %, ties count half

factors.label: Last 16 games
factors.description: Win % over the last 16 games, including last season and playoffs

factors.label: Margin of victory
factors.description: Average point margin over the last 8 games (each capped at 24), including last season and playoffs

factors.label: Quality of results
factors.description: Results over the last 8 games compared with what an average team would do against the same opponents; given Elo and margins, results running ahead of margins tend to fade, so a high value lowers the score

factors.label: Streak
factors.description: Current win or loss streak (ties end it), up to 8, carried across seasons; given the other factors a hot streak tends to fade, so it slightly lowers the score

factors.label: Close-game luck
factors.description: One-score wins minus one-score losses (8 points or fewer) over the last 16 games; close-game luck evens out, so a lucky record lowers the score

factors.label: Getting better (efficiency trend)
factors.description: Recent opponent-adjusted EPA per play (weighted toward the last ~4 games) minus this season's average; given the other factors, an efficiency upswing tends to fade, so it slightly lowers the score

factors.label: QB play (recent starts)
factors.description: Current starting QB's EPA per dropback over his recent starts, on any team; 0 for a QB with under 2 starts or before week 1

factors.label: Vs preseason expectations
factors.description: Win % so far minus the win % expected before the season (Vegas win total 2003-2020, otherwise the model's preseason projection); given the record, beating expectations tends to fade (expectations usually catch up), so it lowers the score

factors.label: Playoff odds trend
factors.description: Change in simulated playoff odds over the last 3 weeks; adds about nothing beyond the other factors (kept so its weight is on record)

holdout.label: Holdout 2022–25 (frozen weights)
holdout.headline: Yes, slightly: better than Elo alone on 2022–25, but within the noise of four seasons.

notes.text: Hot records mostly fade. Once Elo and point margins are known, a strong recent record, a winning streak and close-game wins tend not to last, so these weights are negative or about zero: last 16 games −0.21 (same sign in 14 of 19 seasons); streak −0.03 (same sign in 12 of 19 seasons); close-game luck −0.35 (same sign in 19 of 19 seasons).

The efficiency trend has a small but consistent negative weight (−0.33, same sign in 19 of 19 seasons): once the other factors are known, an efficiency upswing slightly fades. Adding it on top of the factors before it changed the walk-forward rank correlation by −0.0001.

“Vs preseason expectations” has a large, mostly consistent negative weight (−1.22, same sign in 18 of 19 seasons): given the record, beating expectations tends to fade. Expectations come from Vegas win totals for 2003–2020 and from the model’s own preseason projection otherwise, including all of 2021 onward. Pre-registered holdout check: with this factor zeroed the score’s rank correlation is 0.4846, against 0.4853 for the full score (+0.0032 vs Elo alone).

The walk-forward numbers (2003–21) refit the weights each season on earlier seasons only, with unrounded weights: rank correlation 0.5262 for the feel-good score vs 0.5132 for Elo alone. The holdout uses the one frozen, rounded set.
Play-by-play for 1999–2000 is low-confidence, so the efficiency and QB inputs are rougher for those seasons.
Playoff odds come from a simulation with simplified tiebreakers, so close races can be off by a little.

Holdout 2022–25: Over the next 4 games instead of 8, the score − Elo rank-correlation difference was −0.0014 (95% interval −0.0187 to +0.0161 by season blocks, −0.0234 to +0.0203 by team-season). On single games the score was slightly worse than Elo alone (0.2242 vs 0.2228): next-game Brier difference +0.0014 (lower is better), 95% interval +0.0004 to +0.0030 by season blocks and −0.0018 to +0.0044 by season-week. The season-block interval excludes zero.

The holdout Brier maps (turning a rating gap into a single-game win chance) were fit once on seasons up to 2021, as pre-registered. The score’s weights were fit on those same seasons (1999–21), so its map was fit on in-sample score values and is likely a little too steep: its single-game chances on 2022–25 are expected to be slightly overconfident. Elo’s map was fit on the same seasons, but Elo itself has no weights fit to those results (fixed 538-style update constants and a market-implied home edge), so only its two-number map is in-sample. Read the holdout Brier gap against Elo with that in mind. The walk-forward Brier numbers don’t have this problem: each season’s weights and map use earlier seasons only.

These scores describe how fans should feel. They aren’t betting advice: Vegas spreads still predict single games better (holdout 2022–25 Brier score 0.2097 for the spread vs 0.2242 for the feel-good score; lower is better).

Draft capital over original slots was tested as an offseason term on top of the frozen score. The fitted weight was −0.28, 8/19 walk-forward folds agreed with its sign, and the week-0 change in Spearman was +0.0002, so it didn’t pass the gate and the draft doesn’t move the score (it’s shown as text only). This evidence is training-only walk-forward (2003–2021); the 2022–2025 holdout was already used to judge the in-season score.
